children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Intercontinental Exchange canola futures were higher on Monday morning, coming out of the overnight session with increases.
Crude oil prices spiked after Houthis attacked a key Saudi pipeline. The spillover pushed up values in canola, the Chicago soy complex, European rapeseed and Malaysian palm oil.
As the Canada-United States trade war entered its second week, canola along with its oil and meal have not been targeted.
Alberta reported on Friday that its canola harvest was more than two percent complete with early yields at 37 bushels per acre.
Canola crush margins dropped back by C$4.10 to C$4.55 with the November positions between C$267.35 and C$277.50 per above the futures.
The Canadian Grain Commission reported canola exports for the week ended Sept. 6 improved to nearly 94,000 tonnes. The cumulative tally rose to 704,600 tonnes comparted to 529,500 a year ago.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture maintained its call on Canada's canola output for this year at 22.5 million tonnes.
Statistics Canada is set to issue its first production report of 2026-27 on Wednesday. Recently, Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada projected the canola harvest to be 21.6 million tonnes.
The Canadian dollar was weaker on Monday morning with the loonie dropping to 71.83 U.S. cents, compared to Friday's close of 72.12.
